title: Every cloud resource is deployed from Git
description: Ryan's rule (2026-11-11): nobody creates a cloud resource by hand. Every resource is defined in Git and applied by a pipeline on merge to main (GitHub Actions + OIDC, public repo). Agents use the AWS CLI to read, never to create or change. One exception: the first apply of the pipeline's own wider role cannot come from a pipeline that does not exist yet. Also adopts the resources that were made by hand (the Route 53 zone, the budget, the deploy role stack). Design in project/wiki/infrastructure-pipeline.md. Secret values (the two SSM SecureString parameters) are the person-only exception.

comments.text:
# DRAFT Papyrus epic: A Papyrus deployment needs no hand-made cloud resources

Status: draft for Ryan and the Papyrus session. NOT filed on the PPY board. Humorus build work is paused (see the end).

## What is true today (read from ~/Projects/Papyrus)

- **Pipeline roles:** `infra/pipeline/bootstrap.sh` is run by a person per account. It applies `papyrus-pipeline-approver.yaml` (plan, apply and service roles, optionally the GitHub OIDC provider) and sets the `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID` variable on a repository. Its default `--repo` is AnthusAI/Papyrus, so on another account it redirects our own releases (this is PPY-1a6aa6's comment from Humorus). Later role changes already go through the approval-gated `role-stack-deploy` workflow.
- **Shared stacks:** `infra/pipeline/stacks.json` lists two (monitoring, newsletter sending) and `stack_deploy.py` deploys them from a release, with change sets and Remove/Replace safety checks. The operators stack names `anth.us`.
- **Per-site roles and apps:** the app-shell CDK stack (`infra/amplify-app-shell`) creates each site's Amplify apps, Amplify service role (AdministratorAccess), compute role, authoring role and `<siteId>-github-deploy` / `-github-ci` roles. The docs show a person running `cdk deploy`. The account-level `GithubOidcProviderStack` is also deployed by a person after checking the provider list by hand.
- **Edge:** `infra/edge/*.yaml` (CloudFront for anth.us and others) appear to be applied by hand; to confirm.
- **Backend:** AppSync, storage and Lambda are created inside the CMS app by `ampx pipeline-deploy` during the Amplify build. That is already pipeline-driven.
- **Account facts a person provides today:** CDK bootstrap, the Route 53 zone, SES, the Google OAuth client, secret values, registrar name servers.

## Duplication to avoid

A Humorus-only pipeline would duplicate the zone, certificate and edge stacks that Papyrus owns, and `stack_deploy.py`. Humorus has a working draft (unmerged branch `infra/pipeline`) of an import-aware change-set deployer, three least-privilege roles and the DNS, budget, certificate and SES templates. The generic parts belong in Papyrus; see "What is Humorus-specific".

## Epic

**A Papyrus deployment needs no hand-made cloud resources.** Parent of PPY-1a6aa6 (fold it in as the story "works for a second organisation"). Rule (Ryan, 2026-11-11): every cloud resource is defined in Git and applied by a pipeline on merge; agents read with the AWS CLI and never create or change. The person-only steps are the registrar name servers, the Google OAuth client, secret values, and the one seed apply.

### Story 1: A new deployment's account is seeded from a template

```gherkin
Feature: An account is seeded from a template, not a script

  Scenario: One command seeds a new account
    Given a new AWS account and a deployment repository
    When a person applies the account-baseline template once, giving the repository, region, domain and budget as parameters
    Then the account has the GitHub OIDC provider, the plan, deploy, approval and service roles, and a monthly budget
    And nothing in the template names AnthusAI, anth.us or another deployment's account
    And no repository variable of any other repository is written

  Scenario: The seed is the same template the pipeline later updates
    Given a seeded account
    When the template changes in Git
    Then the pipeline updates the same stack, and does not create a second one
```

### Story 2: The pipeline deploys its own roles and account stacks on merge

```gherkin
Feature: Merge deploys the account's stacks

  Scenario: A merge to the release branch applies changed stacks
    Given a stack template changed in a commit merged to the release branch
    When the Deploy workflow runs
    Then it signs in with GitHub OIDC and creates a change set per changed stack
    And it executes only change sets that remove or replace nothing that is not allow-listed

  Scenario: Changing the pipeline's own roles needs an approval
    Given a merged change to the pipeline roles stack
    When the workflow reaches it
    Then it waits for a person to approve the protected GitHub environment
    And the ordinary deploy role cannot change that stack

  Scenario: A pull request shows the plan with read-only access
    Given a pull request that changes a stack
    When CI runs
    Then the templates are linted with no AWS access and the plan is read with a role that can create nothing
```

### Story 3: Hand-made resources in the running Anthus deployments are imported, not replaced

```gherkin
Feature: Existing resources join the pipeline in place

  Scenario: A hand-made zone, role or provider is imported
    Given a resource that was made by hand and is in use
    When the pipeline first manages it
    Then the change set shows Import and no Add, Modify or Remove of that resource
    And the resource has DeletionPolicy and UpdateReplacePolicy Retain
    And for a Route 53 zone the name servers are the same before and after

  Scenario: Nothing is imported until a person has seen the change set
    Given an import of a production resource
    Then the first run stops at the change set for approval
```

### Story 4: It works for a second organisation (PPY-1a6aa6 becomes this story)

```gherkin
Feature: A deployment in another organisation needs nothing from ours

  Scenario: Bootstrapping touches only the new deployment
    Given an account in another AWS organisation and its own repository
    When the account is seeded
    Then the roles trust only that repository
    And no variable, domain or account of the Anthus deployments is read or written
```

### Story 5: It works for a client-owned account (the managed offer)

```gherkin
Feature: A client grants access with one stack

  Scenario: The client launches one stack
    Given a client with their own AWS account
    When they launch the access stack from a link, giving a deployment name
    Then it creates one role our pipeline can assume, requiring an external id, with the same permission ceiling as the seeded roles
    And the client can delete the stack to revoke all access

  Scenario: Our pipeline does the rest
    Given the access stack exists
    When we merge a change in the operating repository
    Then the pipeline seeds the baseline and deploys the stacks in the client's account
    And the client's data and keys stay in the client's account
```

### Story 6: The only person-only steps are the ones nothing can automate

```gherkin
Feature: What a person still does

  Scenario: The list is short and written down
    Given a new deployment
    Then a person does only: apply the seed once, give the registrar the name servers, create the Google OAuth client, and put secret values (for example SSM SecureString parameters, which CloudFormation cannot create)
    And everything else is done by the pipeline
```

### Story 7 (design, built last): Accounts are seeded from the organisation

Design in the next section. Gherkin once agreed:

```gherkin
Feature: New accounts arrive seeded

  Scenario: A new account in the Papyrus OU gets the baseline
    Given an account created in the Papyrus deployments OU
    When it joins the OU
    Then the organisation delivers the baseline stack automatically
    And the account's pipeline can deploy without a person touching it
```

## Organisation-level seeding design (layer 2, design only)

1. **Account creation as code.** A small private organisation repo, deployed by its own pipeline running in the management account, declares accounts with `AWS::Organizations::Account` (name, email alias, parent OU). Creating or moving an account is a merge. The pipeline in the management account uses a narrow GitHub OIDC role created once.
2. **Seeding.** In the management account, a service-managed CloudFormation StackSet carries the account baseline (OIDC provider, plan/deploy/approval/service roles, budget, alarm topic) and targets the OU "Papyrus deployments" with automatic deployment, so any account that joins the OU gets the baseline with no human step. Parameters (repository, domain, budget) come per account: either per-account StackSet parameter overrides declared in the org repo, or a small stack in the new account that the baseline's deploy role then updates. The baseline's deploy role trust names that account's deployment repository.
3. **Ongoing changes.** After seeding, the deployment pipeline owns the account's stacks as in Story 2. The StackSet owns only the baseline; changing it is a merge to the org repo.
4. **Managed offer, client-owned account.** The client is not in our organisation, so no StackSet. They launch the single access stack (Story 5). Same baseline template, delivered by our pipeline through the assumed role instead of StackSets.
5. **Read-only everyday access (proposal, not applied).** In IAM Identity Center (DataParade management account) make a ReadOnly permission set the everyday assignment for people and agents (agents use the AWS CLI to read). Keep AdministratorAccess as a separate break-glass permission set: assigned only to named admins, short session (one hour), and its use alerted. Removing standing admin assignments from the Humorus account is a change in the management account and needs Ryan.

### Who must do the one-time org setup, and cost

- **Who:** an administrator of the DataParade management account (Ryan, and the second admin if he keeps access): enable trusted access for CloudFormation StackSets with Organizations, create the OU, create the OIDC provider and the org pipeline's role in the management account (the one hand-made apply for the whole organisation), assign Identity Center permission sets.
- **Cost, to my knowledge (verify against current AWS pricing before deciding):** AWS Organizations, CloudFormation StackSets, IAM roles, the OIDC provider and Identity Center have no charge of their own. Per account the baseline is free apart from the budget (the first budgets are free; action-enabled budgets beyond the free ones cost cents a day). Costs appear only for what the deployments themselves run: each Route 53 hosted zone is about 0.50 USD a month plus queries, plus Amplify, AppSync, Lambda and storage as today. No Control Tower is proposed, to avoid its extra services.
- **Risk:** the management account becomes the highest-trust place; the org pipeline role must be least-privilege (Organizations, StackSets only) and the repo protected.

## What is Humorus-specific

- Its configuration: the TheHallucinator.ai zone, budget name and limit, site id, repository name, and the GitHub variables that hold them.
- Importing its three hand-made things (the zone, the budget, the `humorus-github-deploy` stack) once Papyrus provides the import mechanism; the registrar name servers (verified unchanged: ns-167.awsdns-20.com, ns-1548.awsdns-01.co.uk, ns-1030.awsdns-00.org, ns-906.awsdns-49.net).
- The two SSM SecureString parameters (`/papyrus/the-hallucinator/openai-api-key`, `/papyrus/shared/typesafe-api-key`): person-only.
- Everything else (the deployer, role templates, zone/certificate/SES templates, the PR plan job) is generic and should live in Papyrus: extend `stack_deploy.py` with import support rather than adding a second deployer.

## What I paused

- Board: epic HUM-be87f4 and its stories/tasks stay as planned work but are set back to open; HUM-2ccd58 holds only this design.
- Code: nothing merged. Branch `infra/pipeline` (pushed, no PR) has: `infra/stacks/*.yaml` (github-deploy widened with deploy/plan/roles-apply/service roles; dns, budget, certificate and SES slots), `infra/stacks.json`, `infra/pipeline/deploy.py` plus 41 passing tests, and an unfinished edit to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (infra lint and read-only plan jobs). The deploy workflow and README were not written. Nothing was applied to AWS.
- Comment added on PPY-1a6aa6 (pushed to Papyrus develop).
- Read-only AWS findings (no IDs): the zone has only NS and SOA records, no tags, and its four name servers match the registrar's; the budget `papyrus-production-monthly` is 200 USD monthly with 50% and 80% actual and 100% forecast alerts to one email subscriber; the CDKToolkit stack exists (hand-made too); open question: CloudFormation import identifiers for `AWS::Budgets::Budget` (primary identifier `Id`, format unknown) must be confirmed; the first IMPORT change set will show whether it works, and the fallback is a person-approved recreate of the budget.
